text:
Let $R_{1} = {(a, b)$ $\in$ N $\times$ N : |a $-$ b| $\leq$ 13} and

$R_{2} = {(a, b)$ $\in$ N $\times$ N : |a $-$ b| $\neq$ 13}. Then on N :
options: Neither $R_{1}$ nor $R_{2}$ is an equivalence relation
$R_{1}$ is an equivalence relation but $R_{2}$ is not
$R_{2}$ is an equivalence relation but $R_{1}$ is not
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$R_{1}=\{(a,b)\in N\times N:|a-b|\leq 13\}$ and

$R_{2}=\{(a,b)\in N\times N:|a-b|\neq 13\}$

In $R_{1}:\because |2-11|=9\leq 13$

$\therefore (2,11)\in R_{1}$ and $(11,19)\in R_{1}$ but $(2,19)\notin R_{1}$

$\therefore R_{1}$ is not transitive

Hence $R_{1}$ is not equivalence

In $R_{2}:(13,3)\in R_{2}$ and $(3,26)\in R_{2}$ but $(13,26)\notin R_{2}$
 
$(\because |13-26|=13)$

$\therefore R_{2}$ is not transitive

Hence $R_{2}$ is not equivalence.

text: The number of ways to distribute 30 identical candies among four children $C_{1}, C_{2}, C_{3}$ and $C_{4}$ so that $C_{2}$ receives at least 4 and at most 7 candies, $C_{3}$ receives at least 2 and at most 6 candies, is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $C_{2}$ receive $c_{2}\in \{4,5,6,7\}$ candies and $C_{3}$ receive $c_{3}\in \{2,3,4,5,6\}$ candies.

The remaining $30-c_{2}-c_{3}$ candies go to $C_{1}$ and $C_{4}$ without restriction: $C_{1}$ can get $0,1,\ldots ,30-c_{2}-c_{3}$, so there are $31-c_{2}-c_{3}$ ways.

Summing over the $4\times 5=20$ pairs $(c_{2},c_{3})$, each $c_{2}$ occurs with 5 values of $c_{3}$ and each $c_{3}$ with 4 values of $c_{2}$:

$\sum\limits _{c_{2}=4}^{7}\sum\limits _{c_{3}=2}^{6}(31-c_{2}-c_{3})=20\times 31-5(4+5+6+7)-4(2+3+4+5+6)$

$=620-110-80=430$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text:
The term independent of x in the expansion of 

$(1-x^{2}+3x^{3})\left (\frac{5}{2}x^{3}-\frac{1}{5x^{2}}\right )^{11},x\neq 0$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
General term of Binomial expansion $\left (\frac{5}{2}x^{3}-\frac{1}{5x^{2}}\right )^{11}$ is

$T_{r+1}={}^{11}C_{r}.\left (\frac{5}{2}x^{3}\right )^{11-r}.\left (-\frac{1}{5x^{2}}\right )^{r}$

$={}^{11}C_{r}.\left (\frac{5}{2}\right )^{11-r}.\left (-\frac{1}{5}\right )^{r}.x^{33-5r}$

In the term,

$\left (1-x^{2}+3x^{3}\right )\left (\frac{5}{2}x^{3}-\frac{1}{5x^{2}}\right )^{11}$

Term independent of x is when

(1) $33-5r=0$

$\Rightarrow r=\frac{33}{5}\notin$ integer

(2) $33-5r=-2$

$\Rightarrow 5r=35$

$\Rightarrow r=7\in$ integer

(3) $33-5r=-3$

$\Rightarrow 5r=36$

$\Rightarrow r=\frac{36}{5}\notin$ integer

$\therefore$ Only for r = 7 independent of x term possible.

$\therefore$ Independent of x term

$=-\left ({}^{11}C_{7}\left (\frac{5}{2}\right )^{4}.\left (-\frac{1}{5}\right )^{7}\right )$

$=-\left (\frac{11.10.9.8}{4.3.2.1}.\frac{5^{4}}{2^{4}}.-\frac{1}{5^{7}}\right )$

$=\frac{11.10.3}{2^{4}.5^{3}}$

$=\frac{11.3}{2^{3}.5^{2}}$

$=\frac{33}{200}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text: If n arithmetic means are inserted between a and 100 such that the ratio of the first mean to the last mean is 1 : 7 and a + n = 33, then the value of n is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$a, A_{1}, A_{2} ........... A_{n}, 100$

Let d be the common difference of above A.P. then

$\frac{a+d}{100-d}=\frac{1}{7}$

$\Rightarrow 7a+8d=100$ ...... (i)

and $a+n=33$ ..... (ii)

and $100=a+(n+1)d$

$\Rightarrow 100=a+(34-a)\frac{(100-7a)}{8}$

$\Rightarrow 800=8a+7a^{2}-338a+3400$

$\Rightarrow 7a^{2}-330a+2600=0$

$\Rightarrow a=10,\frac{260}{7},$ but $a\neq \frac{260}{7}$

$\therefore$ $n=23$

text:
Let f : R $\to$ R be a differentiable function such that $f\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=\sqrt{2},f\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )=0$ and $f^{'}\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )=1$ and 

let $g(x)=\int\limits _{x}^{π/4}(f^{'}(t)\sec t+\tan t\sec tf(t))dt$ for $x\in \left [\frac{π}{4},\frac{π}{2}\right )$. Then $\lim _{x\to \left (\frac{π}{2}\right )^{-}}g(x)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given : $f\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=\sqrt{2},f\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )=0$ and $f^{'}\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )=1$

$\begin{array}{l} g(x)=\int\limits _{x}^{\frac{π}{4}}\left (f^{'}(t)\sec t+\tan t\sec tf(t)\right )dt \\  \\ =[\sec t+f(t)]_{x}^{\frac{π}{4}}=2-\sec xf(x) \end{array}$

Now, $\lim _{x\to \frac{π-}{2}}g(x)=\lim _{h\to 0}g\left (\frac{π}{2}-h\right )$

$=\lim _{h\to 0}2-(\mathrm{cosec}h)f\left (\frac{π}{2}-h\right )$

$=\lim _{h\to 0}\left [2-\frac{f\left (\frac{π}{2}-h\right )}{\sin h}\right ]$

$=\lim _{h\to 0}\left [2+\frac{f^{'}\left (\frac{π}{2}-h\right )}{\cos h}\right ]$

$=3$

text: Let f : R $\to$ R be a continuous function satisfying f(x) + f(x  + k) = n, for all x $\in$ R where k > 0 and n is a positive integer. If $I_{1}=\int\limits _{0}^{4nk}f(x)dx$ and $I_{2}=\int\limits _{-k}^{3k}f(x)dx$, then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f:R\to R$ and $f(x)+f(x+k)=n\forall x\in R$

$\begin{array}{l} x\to x+k \\  \\ f(x+k)+f(x+2k)=n \\  \\ \therefore \quad f(x+2k)=f(x) \end{array}$

So, period of $f(x)$ is $2k$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Now,}I_{1}=\int\limits _{0}^{4nk}f(x)dx=2n\int\limits _{0}^{2k}f(x)dx \\  \\ =2n\left [\int\limits _{0}^{k}f(x)dx+\int\limits _{k}^{2k}f(x)dx\right ] \\  \\ x=t+k\Rightarrow dx=dt\text{(in second integral)} \\  \\ =2n\left [\int\limits _{0}^{k}f(x)dx+\int\limits _{0}^{k}f(t+k)dt\right ] \\  \\ =2n^{2}k \end{array}$

Now, $I_{2}=\int\limits _{-k}^{3k}f(x)dx=2\int\limits _{0}^{2k}f(x)dx$

$I_{2}=2(nk)$

$\therefore l_{1}+nl_{2}=4n^{2}k$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text:
Let x = x(y) be the solution of the differential equation 

$2y\quad e^{x/y^{2}}dx+\left (y^{2}-4xe^{x/y^{2}}\right )dy=0$ such that x(1) = 0. Then, x(e) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given differential equation

$2ye^{\frac{x}{y2}}dx+\left (y^{2}-4xe^{\frac{x}{y2}}\right )dy=0,x(1)=0$

$\Rightarrow e^{\frac{x}{y2}}[2ydx-4xdy]=-y^{2}dy$

$\Rightarrow e^{\frac{x}{y2}}\left [\frac{2y^{2}dx-4xydy}{y^{4}}\right ]=\frac{-1}{y}dy$

$\Rightarrow 2e^{\frac{x}{y2}}d\left (\frac{x}{y^{2}}\right )=-\frac{1}{y}dy$

$\Rightarrow 2e^{\frac{x}{y2}}=-\ln y+c$ ...... (i)

Now, using x(1) = 0, c = 2

So, for x(e), Put y = e in (i)

$2e^{\frac{x}{e2}}=-1+2$

$\Rightarrow \frac{x}{e^{2}}=\ln \left (\frac{1}{2}\right )\Rightarrow x(e)=-e^{2}\ln 2$

text: Let the slope of the tangent to a curve y = f(x) at (x, y) be given by 2 $\tan x(\cos x-y)$. If the curve passes through the point $\left (\frac{π}{4},0\right )$, then the value of $\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}y~dx$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=2\tan x(\cos x-y)$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}+2\tan xy=2\sin x$

$I.F.=e^{\int 2\tan xdx}=\sec ^{2}x$

$\therefore$ Solution of D.E. will be

$y(x)\sec ^{2}x=\int 2\sin x\sec ^{2}xdx$

$y\sec ^{2}x=2\sec x+c$

$\because$ Curve passes through $\left (\frac{π}{4},0\right )$

$\therefore$ $c=-2\sqrt{2}$

$\therefore$ $y=2\cos x-2\sqrt{2}\cos ^{2}x$

$\therefore$ $\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}ydx=\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}(2\cos x-2\sqrt{2}\cos ^{2}x)dx$

$=2-2\sqrt{2}.\frac{π}{4}=2-\frac{π}{\sqrt{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift

text: Let $\vec{a}$ be a vector which is perpendicular to the vector $3\hat{i}+\frac{1}{2}\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}$. If $\vec{a}\times \left (2\hat{i}+\widehat{k}\right )=2\hat{i}-13\hat{j}-4\widehat{k}$, then the projection of the vector $\vec{a}$ on the vector $2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\widehat{k}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $\vec{a}=a_{1}\hat{i}+a_{2}\hat{j}+a_{3}\widehat{k}$

and $\vec{a}\quad .\left (3\hat{i}-\frac{1}{2}\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}\right )=0\Rightarrow 3a_{1}+\frac{a_{2}}{2}+2a_{3}=0$ ..... (i)

and $\vec{a}\times (2\hat{i}+\widehat{k})=2\hat{i}-13\hat{j}-4\widehat{k}$

$\Rightarrow a_{2}\hat{i}+(2a_{3}-a_{1})\hat{j}-2a_{2}\widehat{k}=2\hat{i}-13\hat{j}-4\widehat{k}$

$\therefore$ $a_{2}=2$ ..... (ii)

and $a_{1}-2a_{3}=13$ ..... (iii)

From eq. (i) and (iii) : $a_{1}=3$ and $a_{3}=-5$

$\therefore$ projection of $\vec{a}$ on $2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\widehat{k}=\frac{6+4-5}{3}=\frac{5}{3}$

text: Let the image of the point P(1, 2, 3) in the line $L:\frac{x-6}{3}=\frac{y-1}{2}=\frac{z-2}{3}$ be Q. Let R ($α$, $β$, $γ$) be a point that divides internally the line segment PQ in the ratio 1 : 3. Then the value of 22 ($α$ + $β$ + $γ$) is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Any point of $L$ is $M(3λ+6,2λ+1,3λ+2)$, so $PM\leftarrow =(3λ+5,2λ-1,3λ-1)$.

For the foot of the perpendicular from $P$, $PM\leftarrow$ is perpendicular to the direction $(3,2,3)$ of $L$:

$3(3λ+5)+2(2λ-1)+3(3λ-1)=0\Rightarrow 22λ+10=0\Rightarrow λ=-\dfrac{5}{11}$

So the foot is $M\left (\dfrac{51}{11},\dfrac{1}{11},\dfrac{7}{11}\right )$, and $M$ is the mid-point of $PQ$, i.e. $PQ=2PM$.

$R$ divides $PQ$ internally in the ratio $1:3$, so $PR=\dfrac{1}{4}PQ=\dfrac{1}{2}PM$. Hence $R$ is the mid-point of $PM$:

$R=\left (\dfrac{1+\frac{51}{11}}{2},\dfrac{2+\frac{1}{11}}{2},\dfrac{3+\frac{7}{11}}{2}\right )=\left (\dfrac{62}{22},\dfrac{23}{22},\dfrac{40}{22}\right )$

$22(α+β+γ)=62+23+40=125$

Hence, the answer is 125.

text: Suppose a class has 7 students. The average marks of these students in the mathematics examination is 62, and their variance is 20. A student fails in the examination if he/she gets less than 50 marks, then in worst case, the number of students can fail is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to given data

$\frac{\sum\limits _{i=1}^{7}(x_{i}-62)^{2}}{7}=20$

$\Rightarrow \sum\limits _{i=1}^{7}(x_{i}-62)^{2}=140$

So for any $x_{i}$, $(x_{i}-62)^{2}\leq 140$

$\Rightarrow x_{i}>50\forall i=1,2,3,.....7$

So no student is going to score less than 50.

text: If one of the diameters of the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-2\sqrt{2}x-6\sqrt{2}y+14=0$ is a chord of the circle $(x-2\sqrt{2})^{2}+(y-2\sqrt{2})^{2}=r^{2}$, then the value of $r^{2}$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $x^{2}+y^{2}-2\sqrt{2}x-6\sqrt{2}y+14=0$

$\text{Radius}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{2})^{2}+(3\sqrt{2})^{2}-14}=\sqrt{6}$

$\Rightarrow$ Diameter $=2\sqrt{6}$

If this diameter is chord to

$\begin{array}{l} (x-2\sqrt{2})^{2}+(y-2\sqrt{2})^{2}=r^{2}\text{then} \\  \\ \Rightarrow r^{2}=6+\left (\sqrt{(\sqrt{2})^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}}\right )^{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow r^{2}=6+4=10 \\  \\ \Rightarrow r^{2}=10 \end{array}$

text: If $\lim _{x\to 1}\frac{\sin (3x^{2}-4x+1)-x^{2}+1}{2x^{3}-7x^{2}+ax+b}=-2$, then the value of (a $-$ b) is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{ll} \quad \lim _{x\to 1}\dfrac{\left (\frac{\sin \left (3x^{2}-4x+1\right )}{3x^{2}-4x+1}\right )\left (3x^{2}-4x+1\right )-x^{2}+1}{2x^{3}-7x^{2}+ax+b}=-2 \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & \lim _{x\to 1}\dfrac{3x^{2}-4x+1-x^{2}+1}{2x^{3}-7x^{2}+ax+b}=-2 \\  \\ \Rightarrow  & \lim _{x\to 1}\dfrac{2(x-1)^{2}}{2x^{3}-7x^{2}+ax+b}=-2 \end{array}$

So $f(x)=2x^{3}-7x^{2}+ax+b=0$ has $x=1$ as repeated root, therefore $f(1)=0$ and $f^{'}(1)=0$ gives

$a+b+5\text{and}a=8$

So, $a-b=11$

text:
If the system of linear equations 
$2x-3y=γ+5$, 
$αx+5y=β+1$, where $α$, $β$, $γ$ $\in$ R has infinitely many solutions then the value 
of | 9$α$ + 3$β$ + 5$γ$ | is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
If 2x $-$ 3y = $γ$ + 5 and $α$x + 5y = $β$ + 1 have infinitely many solutions then

$\frac{2}{α}=\frac{-3}{5}=\frac{γ+5}{β+1}$

$\Rightarrow α=-\frac{10}{3}$ and $3β+5γ=-28$

So $|9α+3β+5γ|=|-30-28|=58$

text: Sum of squares of modulus of all the complex numbers z satisfying $z–=iz^{2}+z^{2}-z$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $z=x+iy$

So $2x=(1+i)\left (x^{2}-y^{2}+2xyi\right )$

$\Rightarrow 2x=x^{2}-y^{2}-2xy$ ...(i) and

$x^{2}-y^{2}+2xy=0\ldots (ii)$

From (i) and (ii) we get

$x=0\text{or}y=-\frac{1}{2}$

When $x=0$ we get $y=0$

When $y=-\frac{1}{2}$ we get $x^{2}-x-\frac{1}{4}=0$

$\Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{1\pm \sqrt{2}}{2}$

So there will be total 3 possible values of $z$, which are $0,\left (\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{2}\right )-\frac{1}{2}i$ and $\left (\frac{1-\sqrt{2}}{2}\right )-\frac{1}{2}i$

Sum of squares of modulus

$\begin{array}{l} =0+\left (\dfrac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2}\right )^{2}+\dfrac{1}{4}+\left (\dfrac{\sqrt{2}+1}{2}\right )^{2}+\dfrac{1}{4} \\  \\ =2 \end{array}$

text: Let S = {1, 2, 3, 4}. Then the number of elements in the set { f : S $\times$ S $\to$ S : f is onto and f (a, b) = f (b, a) $\geq$ a $\forall$ (a, b) $\in$ S $\times$ S } is $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $f(a,b)=f(b,a)\geq b$ as well, $f(a,b)\geq \max (a,b)$, and $f$ is fixed by its values on the 10 unordered pairs $\{a,b\}$.

Pairs with maximum 4: $\{1,4\},\{2,4\},\{3,4\},\{4,4\}$, each must map to 4.

Pairs with maximum 3: $\{1,3\},\{2,3\},\{3,3\}$, each maps to 3 or 4.

Pairs with maximum 2: $\{1,2\},\{2,2\}$, each maps to 2, 3 or 4.

The value 1 can come only from $\{1,1\}$, so onto forces $f(1,1)=1$. The value 2 can come only from the two pairs with maximum 2, and 3 must also be attained.

Maximum-2 pairs with at least one value 2: $3^{2}-2^{2}=5$ ways; maximum-3 pairs: $2^{3}=8$ ways; together $5\times 8=40$.

Among these, 3 is not attained when the maximum-2 pairs take values in $\{2,4\}$ with at least one 2 ($2^{2}-1=3$ ways) and all maximum-3 pairs map to 4 (1 way): 3 maps.

Number of functions $=40-3=37$.

Hence, the answer is 37.
